extracted.intended_audience: foundation program officers and staff; minority advocacy organizations and researchers studying philanthropy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for evaluating how responsive U.S. private foundations are to Hispanic needs (grantmaking patterns, institutional policies, applicant preparedness) and for collecting grant data from the Foundation Grants Index. Includes recommendations for foundations and observed applicant weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant data extraction card fields (FGI card)
rubrics_metrics.description: A card designed to extract from the FGI all information desired on grants. Fields: (1) Identification number for the grant as listed in the FGI and year of FGI; (2) Hispanic Group(s) for which grants awarded; (3) Amount; (4) Date when grant was given; (5) Grantee (institution receiving the grant); (6) Information source used by the FGI; (7) Foundation Name; (8) Address; (9) Contact Person (foundation officer as listed in Foundation Directory); (10) Telephone No.; (11) Category - broad category under which the grant is classified (e.g., 'Health', 'Education'); (12) Grant purpose - verbatim transcription of the information provided in the FGI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For future use, revise the card to include a category for 'Recipient Board of Directors' (to indicate whether the grantee's board is at least 50% minority controlled) after the grantee's name, and a sub-category for grants analysis after number 11. The card fields are 'self-explanatory' per the monograph; use verbatim transcriptions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic and minority mailing lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Large foundations should have an Hispanic and other minorities mailing list. If not possible for budgetary reasons, foundations should include a representative group of Hispanic and other minority agencies, institutions and organizations in their regular mailing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing lists are recommended to increase visibility and outreach to minority applicants; foundations unable to maintain separate lists should ensure representative inclusion on existing lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish annual reports and provide application procedure information
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should publish annual reports and provide prospective applicants with detailed information on procedures for the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey found many foundations claim to publish annual reports and to be receptive to inquiries; the monograph notes these claims could not be independently verified, implying the importance of actually making such documentation publicly available and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness in correspondence and decision communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should accept responsibility for reading their mail and responding to letters in a serious manner and should communicate in writing negative decisions to unsuccessful applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being polite and responsive to applicants (including written rejection notices) was reported by foundations but not verified; foundations are advised to formalize these practices to improve transparency and applicant experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide technical assistance and capacity-building to minority applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should devote a small part of their operating budget to offer timely information and technical assistance to minority applicants, particularly in the area of proposal writing, and should offer formal or informal technical assistance to unsuccessful applicants and assistance to strengthen the fund-raising effectiveness of recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report identifies a general lack of such assistance among responding foundations; recommended actions include budgeted TA for proposal development and capacity-building to reduce applicant weaknesses and increase successful grantmaking outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a written affirmative action plan for staff and boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each foundation should set forth in writing an affirmative action plan for increased representation of women and minorities on its staff and Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monograph observes very low Hispanic representation on boards and staff; a written plan is recommended as a concrete institutional policy to improve representative hiring and governance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate, contextual criteria in proposal evaluation (not blind equality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations evaluating proposals should consider more appropriate criteria rather than being blindly 'fair' by giving equal treatment to potential applicants of unequal strength and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommends evaluators apply contextualized standards (e.g., weighting capacity-building needs, applicant track record) instead of strictly identical checklists that disadvantage under-resourced minority applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant preparedness and common applicant weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed weaknesses among minority applicants: applicants do not study and/or adhere to foundation guidelines; proposal contents and structure are poor; minority applicants do not evidence efficient management, budgeting and fund-raising capabilities; applicants do not conduct research on target foundations; applicants do not request and use available technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are anti-patterns funders see in unsuccessful or weak proposals; applicants should address each point (follow guidelines, improve proposal structure, document management/financial capacity, research funders, and seek TA) to improve competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board diversity metric (Hispanic representation on boards/trustees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the number/percent of foundations that have persons of Hispanic origin currently serving as members of Boards of Directors or Trustees and the total number of Hispanic board members represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study reports low counts (e.g., 12 foundations claimed Hispanic directors/trustees with 13 Hispanic board members); board diversity is a measurable indicator of institutional responsiveness and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment diversity metric (full‑time Hispanic employees, consultants, mailing lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the presence of full-time Hispanic employees, use of Hispanic consultants, and whether foundations maintain a Hispanic mailing list; report as counts and percentages of responding foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey found very low figures (e.g., 8.8% employ full-time Hispanics; 16.6% use Hispanic consultants; 10.8% have a Hispanic mailing list). These metrics indicate internal staffing and outreach commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation type and size profile of supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize foundations that support Hispanic needs by type and size (e.g., general-purpose type, medium-sized with assets $1–$25 million, presence of full-time staff; community foundations over-represented, company-sponsored under-represented, small foundations under-represented among respondents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these institutional descriptors to understand which foundation segments are more likely to fund Hispanic programs and to identify gaps in outreach to small and company-sponsored funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of grants per foundation as commitment indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Track how many grants each foundation awards for Hispanic purposes; foundations awarding only one or two grants for Hispanics in a period suggest little or no commitment to the Hispanic sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes 68% of supporting foundations awarded only one or two grants in 1977-78; frequency and repeat grants are indicators of sustained commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant size distribution and concentration metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure distribution of grant amounts (count of grants by size bands, average grant size) and assess concentration: number and dollar share of large grants (e.g., $100,000 and over) versus many small grants (e.g., average of $17,214 across small grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monograph reports 36 large grants accounted for 72% of monies to Hispanics; eight large research grants accounted for 84% of research monies. High concentration suggests funding is dominated by a few large gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of total foundation dollars to Hispanics vs population share
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the percentage of total foundation dollars awarded to Hispanics with Hispanics' percentage of the U.S. population in the same period to assess proportionality of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights disparity: e.g., in 1978 Hispanics represented over 6% of the population but received only 1% of total foundation funds in the surveyed period (with half of that 1% coming from Ford Foundation). This metric signals equity/representation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-of-interest allocation metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down dollars and number of grants to Hispanic beneficiaries by field of interest (e.g., Education, Civil Rights and Legal Services, Research, Community Organization and Development, Health, Social Services, Arts and Humanities, Religion) and note whether a few large grants dominate any field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use percentage shares and counts; the monograph reports Education 30% (but heavily driven by a few Ford Foundation grants), Civil Rights and Legal Services 35% (again concentrated), Research 12% (eight large grants equaling 84% of research monies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess geographic distribution of grant recipients (West, South, Northeast, North Central, National coverage) relative to Hispanic population distribution to identify regional imbalances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: donees in the Southwestern region received the largest percentage of funds, while the Northeast (13% of Hispanic population) received 32% of monies — indicating geographic disproportionality that warrants examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity alignment metric (beneficiaries vs recipient agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabulate dollar values and counts of grants by ethnicity of beneficiaries (Chicano, Puerto Rican, Hispanic, Mixed) and by ethnicity/control of recipient agencies (Hispanic-controlled vs non-Hispanic recipient agencies) to analyze who benefits and which organizations receive funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monograph includes tables breaking down totals and subtotals by beneficiary ethnicity and recipient agency ethnicity; use these to detect whether funds intended for Hispanic beneficiaries are channeled to Hispanic-controlled organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank-ordering foundations by dollar value of grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank foundations by total dollar value of grants to Hispanic programs (assign rank 1 to the foundation making the largest total grant awards) to identify principal funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report uses rank order (e.g., Ford Foundation rank 1) and provides tables of foundations with counts, amounts, and ranks; this reveals concentration and the role of major funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and outreach to minority groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should seek ways to be more visible to minority groups developing programs in their fields of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility includes proactive outreach, publication of procedures, mailing lists, and accessible contact information to increase awareness among potential minority applicants.
